title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 18–19). I is a finite poset of strata. For every flag (chain) d=(i_1<...<i_n) in I there is a space Σ_d. Σ_i is the stratum i, 'unfolded' (déployé) into a manifold with boundary. For d ⊂ d' there are maps Σ_{d'} → Σ_d. When d is an initial segment of d', the map is a fibration, typically a link bundle. When d is cofinal in d' (same last element), the map is an embedding into the boundary. Conditions (b)–(d) on the previous page fix the intersection pattern: Σ_{d∪d'} = Σ_d ∩ Σ_{d'} if d∪d' is a flag, and the intersection is empty otherwise; the boundary pieces are transversal.

This page adds two conditions.
- Condition (e), 'quasi-singularity': the maps Σ_{d'} → Σ_d (in particular Σ_{ij} → Σ_i) are fibrations.
- Condition (f), 'non-singularity': every Σ_i is a manifold with boundary.

Consequences. For i fixed, the Σ_{ji} (j<i) are submanifolds-with-boundary of the boundary ∂Σ_i (written \dot Σ_i). They are the codimension-1 pieces of a 'cylindrical' stratification of ∂Σ_i, indexed by Drap(I_{<i}). More generally, each Σ_d is a manifold with boundary. Its boundary is stratified cylindrically by the Σ_{d'} with d' ⊋ d and d cofinal in d'. By the margin, this index set is in bijection with the nonempty flags of the disjoint union I_{<i_1} ⊔ I_{i_1<·<i_2} ⊔ … ⊔ I_{i_{n-1}<·<i_n}. Equivalently, it is the product of the flag posets of these intervals (flags possibly empty), minus the all-empty tuple. So the Σ_d form a manifold with corners whose face poset is described by flags.

Condition (g), quasi-singular non-singular case. The fibres of Σ_{ij} → Σ_i are manifolds with boundary. The boundary of the fibre is stratified by the Σ_d with d ⊋ (i,j), first element i and last element j, i.e. by Drap(I_{i<·<j}) minus the empty flag. The page first wrote Drap(I_{i…j}) × Drap(I_{>j}) and crossed it out; p.19 settles on the interval-only answer. Consequence drawn on p.19: Σ_{ij} → Σ_i is a fibration with closed-manifold fibres (smooth) iff j is an immediate successor of i.

Purpose. This is the 'dévissage' / 'déploiement' of a tame stratified space into a diagram of manifolds with boundary/corners and link fibrations, indexed by the flag poset (barycentric subdivision) of I. It is a combinatorial model meant to be equivalent to the stratified space with its conical neighbourhoods.
errors: The first index set written for the boundary strata of the fibres of Σ_{ij}→Σ_i, Drap(I_{i<·<j})×Drap(I_{>j}), is wrong: flags beyond j do not lie in the fibre. Grothendieck crosses it out and on p.19 corrects it to Drap(I_{i<·<j}) minus the empty flag.
Indexing conventions waver: Σ_{ji} versus Σ_{ij}, and 'j≠i' versus 'j<i' is struck through. The intended reading is Σ_{ji} ⊂ ∂Σ_i for j<i.
The term 'stratification cylindrique' of the boundary is not defined on this page. The transversality and corner structure it relies on comes from condition (d) and p.18 and is only sketched.

ideas.what: Unfolding (déploiement) of a stratified space into a system of manifolds with boundary Σ_d indexed by flags of the stratum poset, with link fibrations and boundary inclusions
ideas.modern_name: Resolution of a Thom–Mather stratified space to a manifold with corners with iterated fibration structure; 'unzip' of a conically smooth stratified space; 'dépliage' (unfolding)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom (1969) and Mather (1970, control data); Verona (resolution, 1984); Brasselet–Hector–Saralegi (dépliages, ~1991); Albin–Leichtnam–Mazzeo–Piazza (2012); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2017)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (tame topology, the 'dévissage' of stratified structures into manifolds with boundary), only as a programmatic statement without details

ideas.what: Boundary-face poset of Σ_d identified with nonempty flags of I_{<i_1} ⊔ I_{i_1<·<i_2} ⊔ … ⊔ I_{i_{n-1}<·<i_n}, i.e. a product of interval flag posets minus the all-empty tuple
ideas.modern_name: Face poset of the resolved corner of a stratum / depth filtration of boundary hypersurfaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in ALMP and Ayala–Francis–Tanaka; standard combinatorics of subdivided simplices

ideas.what: Criterion: the link bundle Σ_{ij}→Σ_i has closed-manifold fibres iff j is an immediate successor of i
ideas.modern_name: Links between adjacent strata are closed manifolds (no intermediate strata)

missed.claim: This page gives an explicit early (1981–82) axiomatization of what the 'déploiement' of a stratified space should be. It uses flag-indexed manifolds with boundary/corners, fibration axioms (e), non-singularity (f) and the fibre-boundary condition (g), with combinatorial face posets. This predates Verona's and Saralegi's resolutions and the much later ALMP and Ayala–Francis–Tanaka 'unzip' formalisms. The Esquisse only announces it.
missed.quote: les Σ_d=Σ_{i_1…i_n} sont aussi des variétés à bord, et les Σ_{d'} (d'⊋d, d cofinal à d') forment une stratification cylindrique du bord \dot Σ_d de Σ_d
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's priority and concrete form for the resolution/unzip picture of stratified spaces. This is relevant to the history behind the AFT and Lurie exit-path frameworks, though the mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The material is a correct, fairly detailed combinatorial axiomatization of the resolution of stratified spaces to manifolds with corners. It anticipates later work, but the content is now standard (ALMP, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka) and the idea was announced in the Esquisse. What is new is mainly historical detail.
transcription_corrections: 'd commençant [?] d'' should read 'd cofinal à d'' (d cofinal in d'), consistent with p.19.

'dans le cas des strates montrées non singulières' is better read as condition (f), 'non-singularité': '…et dans le cas des conditions de non-singularité impliquent que les Σ_i sont des variétés à bord'.
In the margins and the last line, 'Dép' is more likely 'Drap' (flags): Drap(I_{i<·<j}) × Drap(I_{>j}).
Under the last line, 'drapeaux vides[?]' is likely 'drapeau évent. vide' (possibly empty flag), written under each factor.
Bottom margin: 'il s'identifie à Drap(I_{<i_1} ⊔ I_{i_1<·<i_2} ⊔ … ⊔ I_{i_{n-1}<·<i_n})'.
Line 7: 'Σ_{ji} (j<i) (Drap(I_{<i}))' is the likely reading of the parenthetical, rather than 'disjoints'.
